messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: incident PD-22341 triggered — Canary failure: rollout 'deploy/redwood-v2/2026-03-15' in eu-west-1 showing 5xx spike on inference gateway. Auto-page to oncall. https://pd.example/PD-22341

deploy-bot: deployment event: started rollout deploy/redwood-v2/2026-03-15 -> canary (10%) in eu-west-1 at 4998887700

alex: ack'd oncall page. I'm up — grabbing logs and metrics. :eyes:

maddie: seeing p95 latency jump + error rate ~12% for canary nodes, primarily model shards on node group quant-a. Customers hitting streaming endpoints getting aborted streams.

jay: on it. I'm SSHing into one of the canaries, getting kernel logs and container stdout. quick check: `kubectl -n inference logs deploy/redwood-v2-canary-0 --tail 200`

sam: support queue: two customers opened sev2 tickets mentioning truncated responses, one with partial outputs. I've DM'd their account owners to confirm impact window.

alex: initial mitigation idea: divert canary traffic -> reduce canary to 0% or switch traffic to previous model revision. Do we want immediate rollback or narrow fix?

maddie: metrics look correlated with the new kernel selection path for quantized attention. If we pause traffic to canary, we stop customer impact but lose rollout progress. Recommend traffic diversion to stable and block further canaries.

jay: I pulled relevant logs: ```
[2026-03-15T14:03:21Z] kv_cache: miss_count++
[2026-03-15T14:03:21Z] attention_kernel: fallback_to_generic=true
[2026-03-15T14:03:24Z] runtime: error write to client: broken pipe
```
Looks like kernel fallback thrash causing increased latency then broken streams.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: PD-22341 -> ack by alex at 4998887733

alex: I'm going to pause the rollout (deploy-bot can you execute traffic diversion?). I'll own the incident and coordinate rollback if needed.

deploy-bot: command accepted: `redwood rollout pause deploy/redwood-v2/2026-03-15 --scope=eu-west-1` -> executed at 4998887742

deploy-bot: traffic shift: canary 10% -> 0%, all canary traffic routed to stable revision redwood-v2@2026-03-01 at 4998887751

sam: customers notified: "We've paused a model rollout in eu-west-1 after detecting elevated error rates. We're diverting traffic to a stable revision; service continuity restored for most users. We'll follow up with a post-incident update." Sent to affected account owners at 4998887760

maddie: after diversion, error rate dropped to baseline within one minute. p95 latency back to normal. Monitoring for any residual retries. :white_check_mark:

jay: collecting debug dump for the canary nodes and creating an artifact: `s3://redwood-debug/PD-22341/canary-dump-4998887777.tgz` includes kernel traces and model runtime logs.

alex: good. Next steps: - keep canary paused - gather determinism tests + reproducer on quant kernel - schedule rollback/patch depending on root cause. Who wants the first follow-up?

maddie: I'll start a bisect run against kernel selection flagging commit hashes between 2026-03-01 and 2026-03-15. ETA 2 hours.

jay: I'll try to reproduce locally with the exact seq len profile and quant params. If we isolate, we can ship a hotfix kernel override to avoid fallback path.

alex: great. I'll convert this thread into a short incident timeline and call a quick 15-min bridge in 10 minutes for handoff. If anyone wants to join early, ping me.

incident-bot: Reminder: PD escalation rule in effect. If incident remains unacknowledged by secondary in 10m, page escalates. (But it's already ack'd by alex)

sam: logging timeline and customer messages to the incident doc: https://docs.internal/incidents/PD-22341 — will update with customer lists and communications.

maddie: tagging for postmortem: `sev=2`, root-cause-hypothesis: quant-kernel-fallback-thrash. Also adding test-case id: TC-quant-089

alex: closing immediate mitigation: rollout paused, traffic diverted, customers notified, monitoring stable. Staying on to oversee bisect. If anything changes, I'll update here. Thanks team. :pray:
